name: Lithium diisopropylamide
typicalUses: Quantitative, irreversible formation of kinetic enolates at −78 °C in THF
chemoselectivity: Deprotonates the α-C–H of ketones, esters and nitriles
Bulky and poorly nucleophilic, so it rarely adds to C=O
pitfalls: With an unsymmetrical ketone it gives the less substituted (kinetic) enolate, not the thermodynamic one
Usually made fresh from diisopropylamine and n-BuLi
todoVerify: pKaH of LDA: ~36 is the commonly quoted figure; solvent-dependent

name: Sodium hydride
typicalUses: Deprotonation of alcohols, phenols, 1,3-dicarbonyls and N–H bonds (e.g. Williamson ether synthesis)
chemoselectivity: A strong, non-nucleophilic base that works irreversibly (H₂ escapes)
pitfalls: Although it is a 'hydride', NaH does not reduce carbonyls in normal use: it acts as a base
Sold as a dispersion in mineral oil; reacts violently with water
NaH in DMF or DMSO can undergo dangerous runaway decomposition

name: Potassium tert-butoxide
typicalUses: E2 elimination favouring the less substituted (Hofmann) alkene
Deprotonation of moderately acidic C–H, O–H and N–H
chemoselectivity: Bulky: a poor nucleophile, so it eliminates rather than substitutes
pitfalls: Much stronger in DMSO than in tert-butanol (pKa of t-BuOH ≈ 17 in water, ≈ 32 in DMSO)
todoVerify: pKa of tert-butanol in water (16.5–19 quoted) and DMSO (≈ 32)

name: 1,8-Diazabicyclo[5.4.0]undec-7-ene
typicalUses: Non-nucleophilic base for E2 eliminations
Base in Horner–Wadsworth–Emmons reactions (Masamune–Roush conditions, with LiCl)
chemoselectivity: A strong amidine base: protonation gives a resonance-stabilised amidinium ion
pitfalls: Not completely non-nucleophilic: it can add to very reactive electrophiles

name: Triethylamine
typicalUses: Scavenges HCl in acylations and sulfonylations
Base in Swern oxidations
chemoselectivity: Hindered: a poorer nucleophile than pyridine or DMAP
pitfalls: Forms Et₃NH⁺Cl⁻, which often precipitates from the reaction mixture

name: Pyridine
typicalUses: Base and solvent for acylations (via an acylpyridinium ion)
Ligand in coordination chemistry
chemoselectivity: The lone pair is in an sp² orbital in the ring plane, not part of the aromatic π system, so it is available
pitfalls: A weak base (pKaH 5.2): much weaker than aliphatic amines

name: 4-Dimethylaminopyridine
typicalUses: Nucleophilic catalyst (5–10 mol%) for acylating hindered alcohols
Steglich esterification with DCC
chemoselectivity: The ring nitrogen attacks the acylating agent, giving a very reactive acylpyridinium ion stabilised by the NMe₂ group
pitfalls: Toxic and readily absorbed through the skin

name: n-Butyllithium
typicalUses: Deprotonation of terminal alkynes and very weak C–H acids; directed ortho-metallation
Lithium–halogen exchange
Making LDA from diisopropylamine
chemoselectivity: Also a strong nucleophile: it adds to aldehydes, ketones and nitriles
pitfalls: When only deprotonation is wanted next to a C=O, use LDA instead
Pyrophoric; slowly attacks THF at room temperature

name: Sodium hydroxide
typicalUses: Saponification of esters
Neutralisation; aldol condensations
chemoselectivity: Saponification is irreversible because the carboxylate is formed
pitfalls: Not strong enough to fully deprotonate a ketone α-C–H (pKa ≈ 19–20): only a small equilibrium amount of enolate forms
todoVerify: Conventions for pKa of water: 15.7 vs 14.0

name: Sodium ethoxide
typicalUses: Claisen condensation; malonic and acetoacetic ester alkylation
E2 elimination (Zaitsev product) from secondary/tertiary halides
chemoselectivity: With primary halides it mostly substitutes (Williamson ether synthesis)
pitfalls: Match the alkoxide to the ester (EtO⁻ with ethyl esters) to avoid transesterification

name: Potassium carbonate
typicalUses: Mild base for alkylating phenols (in acetone or DMF)
Methanolysis of acetates (K₂CO₃/MeOH)
chemoselectivity: Deprotonates phenols (pKa ≈ 10) but not ordinary alcohols (pKa ≈ 16)
pitfalls: Largely insoluble in organic solvents: these reactions are heterogeneous

name: Sodium hydrogencarbonate
typicalUses: Neutralising acid in workups
Test for carboxylic acids (CO₂ effervescence)
chemoselectivity: Carboxylic acids (pKa ≈ 4–5) fizz with NaHCO₃; most phenols (pKa ≈ 10) do not
pitfalls: Amphoteric: HCO₃⁻ is also a weak acid (pKa 10.3)

name: Ammonia
typicalUses: Ligand (e.g. [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺, [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺)
Nucleophile: amides from acyl chlorides or esters; amines from alkyl halides
chemoselectivity: Alkylation of NH₃ with alkyl halides gives mixtures (over-alkylation): Gabriel synthesis avoids this
pitfalls: Liquid NH₃ (b.p. −33 °C) is the solvent for Birch reductions

name: Methylmagnesium bromide
typicalUses: Adds to aldehydes (→ 2° alcohols), ketones (→ 3° alcohols), CO₂ (→ carboxylic acids) and epoxides
chemoselectivity: Esters react twice to give tertiary alcohols: the intermediate ketone is more reactive than the ester
pitfalls: Destroyed by any O–H or N–H (water, alcohols, acids, even terminal alkynes), which give methane
Hindered ketones may be enolised or reduced instead of attacked
